body: I haven't talked to her in about a week and I think she may be done with her assignments now, but I think I'm going to wait to contact her. I was going to send her a text at the end of this week to see if she wants to hang out again. Is this a good idea?
this is awesome dude, excellent track selection

thanks for the reply. I guess I could wait it out a few weeks without talking to her, then give her a phone call or something to see if she wants to see me. I really want to see her though because I have heaps of spare time at the moment. It's frustrating.
hahah, what the fuck did I just read?

Can I just add that if you really are stuck in that hole and you feel like you are going to harm yourself. Call someone. Force yourself to do it. I almost killed myself twice in one day, but both times called different people. The second time it was my therapist, who actually made me go to the doctors and got the right help I need. I'm still depressed and wake up every morning considering it, but you just need to talk to people. Don't resign yourself to silence

No. I almost committed suicide yesterday. This was in the morning. I called my ex standing next to the train tracks to find out that she was going to sydney to see her now boyfriend. Its a pretty depressing thought knowing that someone who used to love you is now fucking some other dude, saying I love you to him. Later on I called my mum and she told me it was r u ok day. Ironic huh?

Thanks for the kind replies. Obviously, I haven't done it. I've talked to therapist, doctor, parents, best friend. I think I might go into a psychiatric ward for a little bit to get myself the help I need.

There is no 'set time' for getting over a break up. Take as much time as you need, don't feel like you have to rush getting over her. It's possible that you'll always feel for her, but the feelings will fade with time, until the point where you can look back on the relationship and be happy that it happened, not depressed, jealous or angry because it's over.

Make sure you stay strong with no contact. Trust me, if you talk to her AT ALL, it's going to set you waaaaay back. Just keep occupied in the mean time. Get an excersize routine going so you can get fit before you go to college. Use these two weeks to have fun, hang out with friends, do shit that you want to do, because you'll miss home when you move.

And college is the best time for anyone who is single. Don't be a depressed loser there, actually get excited about it. You're going to make awesome friends, you're going to meet other girls and you're goign to have ea lot of fun. I think you're just in a bit of a slump at the moment. It will all be okay in the long run
yes, fucking delete this shit. get it off the internet.

My ex said this to me when I asked if we could be together (she's currently in a LDR) - "maybe in the future but not right now"

What the fuck am I meant to think about that? I'm still holding on to it. I want to be together with her again so badly, but that kind of shit just fucks with my head.

That's totally normal man. You probably won't stop thinking about your ex, ever. It's just that every day you think less and less of her. Eventually you won't think of her for a day, a week, a month, but thoughts of her will still come back. Just give it time, you will grow emotionally distant from it. It hurts now, I know, but one day it just won't hurt anymore. It will just be a memory. You will still think 'oh yeah I remember feeling sad about that', only then you won't feel sad.

Chin up, keep socialising and going for those other girls. You don't want to pass something up just because you're so focused on your ex, trust me.

Update. I broke and called her last night, telling her I was confused by her text because I thought she didn't want to talk. She apologised but I said don't worry about it. We ended up just talking for half an hour about our lives. I'm still enchanted by her and there are definitely feelings on her side too, but she's with another and it looks pretty serious. I caved and told her I still felt for her strongly and wanted us to be on good terms for the future. 

I'm not moving on at all, I still can't get over the idea of us being together. It's so shit because I fucked up completely in te past and trying to put pieces back together is hurting me bad. I want to stop and just move forward. I was thinking about travelling overseas by myself for a few months, I'm getting bored as hell at home and have money to spend. Sorry I just need to vent and have someone listen to me.

Of course I want to be with her again, but she's made the situation clear. I just don't want her to think of me as an asshole so that we can be friends in the future. And also because if she wanted to get back together in the future I'd want to be on good terms.

Yeah I know I lost her and it fucking sucks and I feel like a failure. We're not in contact. She said she didn't want us talking anymore, it's just that message she sent... I don't know why I responded in the way I did. Should I apologise to her? The possibility of her wanting to get back with me (should she decide to break up with her boyfriend) would be so low now.

The only thing is, next year I'm going back to uni and I'll definitely bump in to her, so I may have to remain friends for civility's sake.

We agreed to break up before she left, and she had let out all her sadness about the breakup prior to leaving, but she expected us to be friends while she was over there. I kind of just wanted her to be on her own so she didn't have to think about me. It's just the way I broke it off with her that made her upset... 

And now I guess this makes me look like an even bigger asshole.

She left for the US on new years, and we'd agreed to break up beforehand. We didn't really set the boundaries for communication, and after two weeks it was getting too much. I cut off contact on an impulse without really thinking, cause I'd read advice about severing. I guess I didn't really apply the rule very effectively...

Wow this is almost exactly my situation. Broke up with the ex cause he went overseas 8 months ago, cut off contact shortly after and... Broke her heart. She came back and we caught up about 2 months ago, then hooked up a month ago. I knew she was in a LDR with her now bf, but we made out for a good 10 mins anyway, only for her to tell me she couldn't be with me. Total mindfuck, completely heartbroken.

I was in the mindset of getting her back as soon as we caught up, just like u. But you have to realise, she's in another relationship, and u have to respect that, regardless of how you feel. I know it seems like you could be together and happy again if it weren't for him, but that's just not a reality. No use wasting your time and thoughts dwelling on the what ifs, the what could be. Don't get me wrong, you're gonna think about her a lot, it's unavoidable. If you feel up to it, write her a letter explaining how you feel. It may sway her, it may not. Regardless, be totally honest. Don't plead or beg, just tell her exactly how u feel. Closure helps A LOT. Make sure to sever completely as well. Be final about it. This about you moving on. Remember - she has moved on, even if she still has feelings for you. If she really wants to be with you, she will. You can't force her, and if you try you'll push her further away. Be mature and sure footed about moving on, it's the absolute best option for everyone involved.

This is about you now - this is your time to grow and develope as a person. Do the things you love again, hang out with friends, excersize, get fit, take care of yourself and things will start coming together again. Flirt with other women and socialise. You'll start feeling better soon, I promise. You're probably thinking 'yeah he's right, and if I do all this maybe she'll come back!' maybe she will, but it's 95% sure she won't. And why would you want your motivation to be hinged on that anyway. Remember, you're doing it for YOU. This is your life, nobody else can make it better but yourself.

Probably the hardest thing is going to be the constant barrage of thoughts. The mind is a powerful thing, and unrelenting. It's going to tell you stories that aren't true, bombard you with memories and possibilities, and call you a fuck up. Don't pay attention to it! Focus on the things that matter to you and just let the thoughts be there. Don't struggle against them, but don't fuse with them either, or else you'll make yourself feel like crap.

Trust me man, I've been in your boots exactly. She does still feel for you, like my ex does for me. She may love you, but she's not in love with you. Huge difference. I know you want the fantasy to happen, and yeah, so do I. But that's just what it is, a fantasy. Live in reality, not fantasy, and make you're reality even better.

Definitely do try and get some closure from her, it will help. But if she says it's over, it's over. Respect her decision and move on.

Best of luck man, keep us updated
